findings.title: Restore MXCSR explicitly; the new fenv guard does not provide its promised Windows isolation
findings.evidence: Every exported operation uses only fegetenv, fesetround(FE_TOWARDZERO), fesetenv. Retained actual MinGW control evidence at model-handoff-source-e48808f53/eech-campaign/reference/d3-model-characterization/model-mingw-fenv-control-20261030.json exercises this exact sequence: native exit 0, x87 CW restored, MXCSR changes 0x1fb4/0x3fb4/0x5fb4 to 0x7fb4 for RN/RD/RU. Artifact SHA256 5d974842abb337e88b10ae850b37f7d20f91a6721009328fbe3a623489de411b. This is reused toolchain evidence, not a new candidate run.
findings.impact: Calling the new host field from a non-RZ host changes subsequent SSE arithmetic, including on a refusal. The advertised complete x87 CW/SW/MXCSR preservation is false. The Rust test checks a quotient only and does not establish complete control/status preservation.
findings.requested_change: Use the established explicit complete x87/SSE save/set/restore guard (or equivalent) around all kernel exits, including validation failures; preserve status and control, not just rounding. Align documentation with implementation and validate the corrected boundary under actual Windows control/status modes.

findings.title: Validate against an immutable request and enforce the lightning step protocol before consuming RNG
findings.evidence: ENV_BRIDGE invokes provider(request), then consults that same mutable table's want_vector, server and lightning_draw to decide required reply fields. Example: a wind provider executing r.want_vector=false; return {speed=3} passes the bridge for an original vector request; the bridge synthesizes {0,0,0}, which Core accepts. A step answer {need_draw=true,timer=0} also passes for an original client request, and campaign_env_step unconditionally calls frand1. Missing expired is silently defaulted false, and the post-draw answer need not report an expiry.
findings.impact: Malformed providers can silently substitute a zero physical vector, bypass re-ask validation by editing request.lightning_draw, or advance the shared campaign RNG on the client and suppress a lightning event. These are successful accepted replies, not clear refusals.
findings.requested_change: Capture the original request contract before the callback and validate against those immutable values. Permit need_draw only for a server's first expiry negotiation; require the done reply's expired boolean explicitly and enforce the final post-draw expiry state. Apply equivalent checks at the C/Rust provider boundary so direct EnvProvider replies cannot bypass them. Reject malformed answers before RNG consumption or mirror writes.

findings.title: Preserve the original step's short circuits instead of adding blanket input refusals
findings.evidence: The new step rejects all non-finite camera components before selecting the model. The retained original reads no camera in global mode or local radius-zero mode; its weather query uses x/z only, never camera.y. Thus an unused NaN y, or any unused non-finite camera under global mode, now refuses a step the original completes. The new pre-step gust check also imposes [0,1e6), although the original updates then wraps. For example, an imported/set phase -0.25 with delta 5 reaches phase 0.25 in the original without invalid indexing; the new code refuses before that arithmetic. The original float setter has no such precondition.
findings.impact: This structural move changes the accepted domain of existing session/setter/update paths. The 1e6 cutoff is also an arbitrary new boundary, not the original's assertion or wrap condition.
findings.requested_change: Validate only inputs needed by the selected operation/branch, preserving the original evaluation order and supported finite cases. Remove or justify/classify any added phase restriction using the actual post-update wrap domain; do not silently introduce a clamp or change the original wrap arithmetic.
